### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via getMetaItemLayered (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b14235854af543a95de0e7fe2bbb5d1ea012c883` — the merge of head `238b9ee6942a4215fe34b1425ebe92d8b066fc0a` into base `67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b14235854af543a95de0e7fe2bbb5d1ea012c883 && git checkout b14235854af543a95de0e7fe2bbb5d1ea012c883
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94 238b9ee6942a4215fe34b1425ebe92d8b066fc0a && git checkout -B drift-repro 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94 && git merge --no-ff 238b9ee6942a4215fe34b1425ebe92d8b066fc0a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Epic red-line read at `238b9ee694` · 2026-11-12T05:42Z

Head-sha: `238b9ee6942a4215fe34b1425ebe92d8b066fc0a`

**PASS.** Read from the diff, the FROM → TO table and the dev report 6815686715. The seat ran nothing locally. The contract review owes the runs.

- **Red line 1 (resolution never loosened): holds.** Every moved answer is 200 → 409 or `[]` → every holder. No read serves more than before. `judgesPackageLessRows` only widens which types are judged, and a one-holder name still serves its item.
- **Red line 2 (ambiguity reported, never guessed): holds for what the PR touches.** A package-less item of a two-holder `action` or narrowed-type name is refused at both exact addresses, naming both holders. The layered read now judges its code layer and its stored row as the plain read does, so a package-less row is no longer reported as each holder's overlay.
  - Two locations of the same class remain outside this diff, measured by the dev: the draft and preview exits return before `exactQualifierItem`, and `hook`, `job`, `queue`, `sharing_rule` and `assignment_rule` are not judged. Filed as #32568 (one card, both locations), Blocked-by #32407. They do not block this PR: it moves nothing there.
- **Red line 3 (independently releasable): holds.** The four moved answers are declared FROM → TO with their arms and pins. One-holder, bound-row, Regime C, bare-read and code-layer answers are pinned as CONTROLs. The new export is declared under `Clause-②: yes`.
- **Landing.** Merge `main` first (K = 15). A new head after that merge needs only a delta note from this seat if the merge touches `protocol-exact-qualifier.ts` or `protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts`. The conflict with PR #32497 on `stored-package-references.literal-namespace.test.ts` follows the #32407 ruling: the second lander keeps both changes and a pin.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `238b9ee6942a4215fe34b1425ebe92d8b066fc0a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: (no `hits`: narrowing face) + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/stored-package-references.ts

Inputs: card #32407 with its 3 comments (triage 6792792692, claim 6812610051, os-dev-report 6815686715), the PR body, the 8-file list, the net diff against merge-base `e06d04f9`, and the check-runs on the head. The tests, the changeset prose and the rest of the diff are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-11-12T05:45Z: 19 concluded `success`, 0 failed, the rest skipped by path filter. **13 still pending, so they carry no verdict yet:** Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus. This PASS is the contract verdict only. ACCEPT waits for those 13 to conclude green.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`packageLessRowOwners` gate widened from `readsByPackage` to `judgesPackageLessRows` — right.** The new gate is `isPackageScopedType` and (`readsByPackage` is true, or the type is in core's `NAMESPACE_SCOPED_BARE_NAME_TYPES`). On this head that set is `agent`, `skill`, `action`, `email_template`. Three of them are already in `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES`, so on a `SchemaRegistry` the only type whose answer moves is `action`. That is the card's gap exactly.
2. **Plain exact read of `action`, package-less registry item, two holders: 200 to 409 — right.** `exactQualifierItem` (unchanged) reaches `packageLessRowOwners` for a stamp of `undefined`, `''` or `sys_metadata`, and now gets both holders for `action`. One holder returns the item. A bound item returns on its holder only. This is D4 and ruling 6761802819, and it is a narrowing.
3. **List scoped to a holder, `action`: the package-less stand-in row is now withheld — right, and implied rather than written.** `packageLessRowWithheld` (not in the diff) asks the same `packageLessRowOwners`, so the list moves with the gate. The card's Do 2 asks for it.
4. **Layered read `?layers=true&package=X`: 200 to 409 for a package-less stored row of a two-holder name, every judged type — right.** This is a narrowing for the read-set types as well (`email_template` and the rest), not only `action`. The PR's FROM → TO states that.
5. **Layered code layer now passes through `exactQualifierItem` — right.** Another package's item becomes the admitted holder's, or `null`. A package-less runtime item of a two-holder name refuses.
6. **New public export `judgesPackageLessRows` from `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` — right as a widening.** It is a type predicate; see nit N1.
7. **`packageLessRowOwners` on a registry without `readsByPackage`, or one answering `false`, for a narrowed type: `[]` to every holder — right.** It reaches only an embedder's registry or a test double. The PR's FROM → TO declares it.
8. **`os migrate stored-references` lists package-less rows of judged types outside the read set — right.** It is a report and narrows nothing. The walk now starts from `PACKAGE_SCOPED_TYPES` (core, already a dependency of `@objectstack/cli`), filtered by the same predicate the read uses, so the report and the refusal cannot drift apart.
9. **Not moved, checked:** `pairMemberWithheldAt` keeps its `readsByPackage`-only gate, and its jsdoc still says so. `admitExactQualifier` is untouched. Disabled holders are still counted (see ③ item 3).

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/cli` — **matches.** `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing an author can write changes, only whether a read answers. By AGENTS.md step 3, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner. The banner, the FROM → TO with the one-line fix, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) are all in the changeset body. Both moved packages are named. `objectql` gains tests only and is rightly absent.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — **matches**, on the PR body and the changeset alike. `yes` is for the new export, and the one arm is for the reads. The card said `no (narrowing)`; the export is what turns it to `yes`, and the dev declared that deviation. Precedent #32244 was declared the same way.
- Nit N3 below is on the changeset's wording, not its level.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` is empty. The five declared deviations and the two out-of-scope findings follow.

1. **`Metadata-protocol: none` where dispatch expected `narrowed` — answered: agree** (② above).
2. **Plain read declines a stored package-less row of a shipped action (Regime C), while the layered read refuses it — answered: accepted as declared.** The row is served at neither address, so red line 1 holds. The layered read used to attribute the row to each holder, and a refusal is what the card's Do 3 asks for. See N3 for the one condition the prose leaves out.
3. **Disabled holders, the context the seat handed me — verified against the tree.** `packageLessRowOwners` counts every holder that `packageScopedHoldersOf` returns, disabled ones included. This PR does not touch that, but it does carry the over-count to `action`: a disabled holder beside an enabled one makes the enabled holder's exact read refuse. Ruling A on #32183 puts the exclusion in #32497's hunk. PR #32497 is open and unmerged at this read, so neither has landed. The PR body carries the serial sentence, names #32497, and quotes the ruling verbatim, including the duty of the second lander (both effects at the layered merge point, plus one pin). **Sufficient.** The seat holds the second lander to it.
4. **Out-of-scope finding 1 (the strict draft read and `previewDrafts` return before `exactQualifierItem`) — honestly out of scope, but it must not stay at "carrier: none".**
   - Verified by reading: in `protocol-meta-item-reads.ts` the draft arm returns well before the `exactQualifierItem` call near the end of step 3.
   - It predates this card and holds for read-set types (`email_template`), which #32214 owned. The card's Do speaks of the served active item. So routing it out is honest.
   - **One face is missing from the dev's finding:** the `draft` layer of `getMetaItemLayered` (`withDraft`), inside the function this PR edits. It reads `findServedOverlayRow` with `state: 'draft'` at the named package and is not judged either. It mirrors the strict draft read by contract, so fixing it alone here would break that parity. It belongs on the same follow-up card.
   - **Escalated to the seat:** file one card naming all three faces (strict draft read, `previewDrafts`, layered `draft` layer) before this card closes. It is the same defect class as red line 1, behind draft-read admission.
5. **Out-of-scope finding 2 (`hook`, `job`, `queue`, `sharing_rule`, `assignment_rule` have no one-holder rule) — honestly outside the card's Do, but inside the card's own gap sentence. Escalated.**
   - Verified: none of the five is in `BARE_NAME_ONE_HOLDER_TYPES`, `NAMESPACE_SCOPED_BARE_NAME_TYPES` or `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES`. All five are in `PACKAGE_SCOPED_TYPES`, so `admitExactQualifier` admits `?package=X` for them and `judgesPackageLessRows` answers `false`.
   - Do 1 lists types that are "already narrowed, or will be". These five were never narrowed, because they never had the rule. So the dev's reading of the Do list is correct, and the unit CONTROL pins `hook` as unjudged on purpose.
   - But the card's gap section ends with "The same holds for any other package-scoped type outside the read set", and these five are that case, live on `main`.
   - Whether D4 judges a type with no one-holder rule is an epic question, not this dev's. **Escalated to `epic:#31527`** for a ruling and a card. "Measured, not filed" is not an end state.
6. **No assignee or review request on the PR — answered:** process only, no contract effect.

### ④ Design judgment

No `hits` on this face. The narrowing is judged against the published rule (ADR-0150 D4, ruling 6761802819, the card), and each implementing file against the code it cites. **No must-fix and no should-fix.**

**The narrowing itself.** It makes the rule's own refusal real and takes no declared capability away. A package-less item of a two-holder name is no holder's own under D4. `action` was serving it at both exact addresses, which is the class red line 1 forbids. One holder, and a bound item, answer as before. Tying the gate to `NAMESPACE_SCOPED_BARE_NAME_TYPES` is the right hinge: `webhook`, `connector` and `flow` join the refusal in the very change that narrows them, which is what ruling 6761802819 requires ("in place before a type narrows") and what the card's Serial section relies on.

**`protocol-exact-qualifier.ts`** — agrees with its contract.
- The `judgesPackageLessRows` jsdoc matches the body clause for clause. `function` answers `false` because it is not a package-scoped metadata type.
- `packageLessRowOwners` keeps the platform-requested-name exception after the gate.
- The `exactQualifierItem` jsdoc is updated to the widened rule.
- Tried to break it:
  - A type in the read set on a registry answering `false` now names holders. This is intended and declared.
  - The exact-read path is unaffected by a registry lacking `packageScopedHoldersOf`, because `exactQualifierRegistry` guards it.
  - `pairMemberWithheldAt` was deliberately left on `readsByPackage`, and its jsdoc says so. `action` is not a bundled type, so no pair-member row of it exists to diverge.

**`protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts`** — agrees with its contract.
- The stamp is `served.overrideOf ?? row.package_id` through `withRowBinding`. That is the same binding the plain read states for the row it serves (`protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`: `_packageId: served.overrideOf`, else `withRowBinding(item, recPkg)`).
- Walked every arm of `exactQualifierItem` with that stamp:

  | Row | Result |
  |---|---|
  | Package-less, two holders | throws 409 naming both |
  | Package-less, one holder | kept |
  | Bound to the address | kept |
  | Declared override of the address's base | kept |
  | Pair row owned elsewhere | `overlay`, `overlayScope` and `overlayRow` cleared together |

- The raw row is still what `overlay` reports; the stamped copy is only judged.
- The code-layer line turns `undefined` into `null`, so the degraded-service check after it still fires correctly.
- The refusal precedes the Regime C decline here. That is the declared divergence in ③ item 2.

**`index.ts`** — one export added beside its siblings, and nothing removed.

**`stored-package-references.ts`** — agrees. The module doc names the widened set and the predicate. The type list comes from the same predicate the refusal uses. `registry.readsByPackage` stays optional and is read through `?.`. The `email_template` listing is unchanged, since it is in both sets.

**Nits** (none affects correctness or the contract):

- **N1 (nit), `protocol-exact-qualifier.ts`.** `judgesPackageLessRows` is declared as the type predicate `type is PackageScopedType`, but its `false` answer depends on the registry, not on the type alone. A caller holding a `PackageScopedType` would see the `false` branch narrowed to `never`. No caller in the tree branches that way: the CLI uses it in a `filter`, and `packageLessRowOwners` returns early. A plain `boolean` return would be the honest signature. Left as a follow-up.
- **N2 (nit), `protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts`, by reading, not reproduced.** The new comment says "A pair's row the address does not own is not its layer". After `overlay` is cleared, the pre-existing orphan block further down can report that same pair row again as a shadowed `overlay` with `effective` equal to `code`, when it is stored in a pair of the address's base. That is the orphan block's own older contract (reported, never served), and the outcome is strictly better than before, when the row was `effective`. The comment could say "is not its served layer".
- **N3 (nit, changeset and PR prose).** The sentence "a stored package-less row of an action a package ships is still declined … so the plain read keeps serving the holder's own action" is true only while the row is not hydrated into the registry's bare slot. Once boot or a list read hydrates it (stamp `''` or `sys_metadata`), it is the "environment item" of the changeset's item 1, and the plain read answers 409. The dev's own measurement and the three-stamp pin say this, but the two sentences are never joined. So the same stored row can answer 200 before hydration and 409 after. That dependence on hydration predates this PR (`getItem` answers the bare slot first, and `isStoredFlowEntryOfShippedName` is flow-only), and this PR makes the hydrated branch safe. Follow-up: one clause in the prose, and the seat may want a card on the plain read answering one way regardless of hydration.
